source.note: Vectors are hand-derived deterministic encodings from the accepted normative documents — NOT from the prototype's throwaway BRIEF.md wire format, and not from any implementation encoder. Signature values were computed once with the fixture-fixed test keys (test-keys.json) and are replayed by verification only.

framing.control: u32 big-endian length | protobuf Frame (spec §3); length 0 or > 65536 -> 401
framing.media: 24-byte big-endian header | PCM payload on QUIC DATAGRAM (spec §7.1); NOT length-prefixed

error_registry_coverage_notes.102: unreachable in v2.0: 102 is for a KNOWN capability the Server cannot honor, and no capability ids are assigned in v2.0 (spec §4.5); unknown ids are ignored (see control.negotiate-unknown-capability-ignored). The first reviewed spec revision that assigns an id must add its 102 vector.
error_registry_coverage_notes.205: no wire bytes exist: 205 is the Client's LOCAL classification of a TLS-handshake pin mismatch (spec §3, §6.2) — it never appears as a control frame.
error_registry_coverage_notes.206: timing-only: PAIRING_PENDING_TIMEOUT fires after the 10-minute pairing deadline (Error(206)+Close(206)); no bytes to pin beyond the codes.
error_registry_coverage_notes.503: no wire sequence is pinned by the accepted spec for SERVER_STOPPING (no §5.2 row); left to the maintainer rather than invented (spec gap noted in test-keys.json derivation_assumptions is not required for this one — simply unspecified).

cases.summary: Paired-client authentication: the full 4-message signed-challenge exchange, ending in AuthResult(OK) with a Server-assigned session_id.
QR pairing, full 4-message flow including PairingConfirm.client_proof; the Server persists the identity only after verifying binding_echo and client_proof, then returns PairingResult(OK).
SAS pairing (no camera): the same 4-message flow with PAIRING_MODE_SAS, no pairing_nonce anywhere; admission is the administrator-enabled local pairing window.
Version/capability negotiation with the canonical (empty) v2.0 capability sets, answered OK; the Server then pushes the current ConfigurationPublished, moving the session to READY.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/pairing.md §6.3 (canonical form: count(u8) || id(u32 BE) ascending)
cases.summary: A well-formed but unknown capability id is IGNORED, not rejected: the canonical single-id list [7] is accepted and the honored intersection echoed back is empty.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (READY subscribe row; PLAYING unsubscribe row: StreamEnded first, then UnsubscribeResponse)
cases.summary: The subscribed-session happy arc: Subscribe is answered with the current Configuration, the active stream is announced (StreamStarted push), the Client reports a full PlaybackDiagnostics snapshot, and Unsubscribe in PLAYING produces StreamEnded(502, 'unsubscribed') BEFORE UnsubscribeResponse.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.4 (validation table: Frame without a body set -> 401)
cases.summary: An unknown oneof case (unknown message type) at Frame level: the Frame decodes, but the unknown field never sets body, so the Frame is 'without a body set' -> Error(401)+Close(401).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.4 (validation table: unknown proto3 fields ignored)
cases.summary: An unknown field alongside a valid body is ignored under the standard evolution rule: the Subscribe inside is processed normally.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.4 invariant 2 (subscription cannot complete before READY)
cases.summary: State violation: a Subscribe arriving before READY (here: in NEGOTIATING, before Negotiate) is answered with the fatal pair Error(402)+Close(402).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §6.2 (402 INVALID_STATE: request illegal for the current state)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.4 invariant 1 (every request answered exactly once)
cases.summary: State violation: AuthInit sent in READY (a fully set-up session) — illegal for the current state, answered with fatal Error(402)+Close(402).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.4 (validation table: capabilities duplicated or not ascending -> 401)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/pairing.md §6.3 (canonical form: ascending numeric order, unique)
cases.summary: A Negotiate whose capabilities list is not in ascending numeric order ([2, 1]) is malformed: Error(401)+Close(401).
Version conflict: Negotiate with protocol_major = 1 is refused with Error(101)+Close(101).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (PairingConfirm: binding_echo mismatch or client_proof invalid -> PairingResult(201)+Close(201))
cases.summary: Pairing with a wrong client_proof: binding_echo verifies, but the 64-byte proof signature does not (one byte flipped) — nothing is persisted, PairingResult(201)+Close(201).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (AuthProof valid, identity matches no record -> AuthResult(202))
cases.summary: Valid signature, unknown identity: the exchange completes with AuthResult(202) — pair first; the connection stays open and the Client may try another stored pairing.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (AuthProof signature invalid -> AuthResult(203); 5th failure -> Close(203))
cases.summary: Invalid signature: the AuthProof is the happy-path signature with one bit flipped in s — verification fails, AuthResult(203) is sent and the failure counted.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §6.2 (204 AUTHORIZATION_DENIED: retryable=no, re-pairing=no — admin action)
cases.summary: Valid signature, revoked identity: AuthResult(204) — the denial is an admin matter, not a re-pairing matter.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (any: fatal error raised -> matching Error + Close)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §6.2 (revocation-driven close of an active session uses 204 within <= 5 s)
cases.summary: Revocation of a live session: the operator revokes the Client identity while its session is PLAYING; within <= 5 s the session receives the fatal pair Error(204)+Close(204).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (CONNECTING: capacity exceeded -> transport close carrying 301)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (32 established sessions, TM-2; 16 concurrent handshakes, TM-1)
cases.summary: Server at capacity: the connection is refused BEFORE any control frame exists — signaled ONLY by the QUIC application close code 301 (no Error frame, no Close frame).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (source-address auth-failure rate exceeded -> Close(302); pairing failure rate -> Close(302))
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (20 auth failures per sliding 60 s per source; 5 pairing failures; 8 outstanding requests)
cases.summary: Rate limiting: once a source address exceeds the failure budget, the Server answers with Close(302) (this vector shows the final Close; the budget buildup is precondition, not wire bytes).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (AUTHENTICATING: supersede — the older session of the same identity is closed with Close(303))
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (one active session per Client identity, TM-3)
cases.summary: Same-identity supersede: a second connection authenticates the same Client identity; the OLD connection is closed with Close(303) (Close only — the §5.2 row names no paired Error).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §3 (framing: length == 0 -> Error(401)+Close(401), before any allocation)
cases.summary: Framing violation: a length prefix of 0 declares a zero-length Frame — refused before allocation.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §3 (framing: length > 65536 -> Error(401)+Close(401), before any allocation)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (control frame size 64 KiB hard cap)
cases.summary: Framing violation: a length prefix declaring 65537 bytes — one over the 64 KiB cap — is refused on the prefix alone, before any body bytes are read or allocated.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.1 (a Frame with no body set is malformed — 401)
cases.summary: A non-empty Frame that never sets the oneof: a single unknown field (field 15) is ignored, leaving body unset -> Error(401)+Close(401).
Undecodable bytes inside a correctly length-delimited frame: field 1 (AuthInit) declared with wire type 2 and length 255, but only 1 byte follows — the parse fails.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.4 (validation table: PairingRequest capabilities duplicated or not ascending -> 401)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/pairing.md §6.3 (canonical form: unique, ascending numeric order)
cases.summary: PairingRequest with a duplicated capability id ([3, 3]): no canonical form exists, the list is malformed -> Error(401)+Close(401), not a 201 pairing rejection.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/pairing.md §6.3 (a list with more than 255 ids is malformed and fails pairing with the malformed-message code)
cases.summary: PairingRequest carrying 256 ascending unique capability ids (1..256): the canonical count field is a u8, so the list has no canonical encoding -> Error(401)+Close(401).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.4 (validation table: Configuration invalid -> receiving side Error(401)+Close(401))
cases.summary: Invalid Configuration pushed to the Client: codec CODEC_UNSPECIFIED with otherwise-valid PcmParameters — the receiving side answers Error(401)+Close(401).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (PLAYING: duplicate Subscribe -> non-fatal Error(402, retryable=false), connection maintained)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (error response classes: the non-fatal Error class)
cases.summary: The non-fatal 402: a duplicate Subscribe in PLAYING gets Error(402) ONLY — no Close, connection kept, state unchanged; the next request is still served, which the follow-up RequestConfiguration proves.
A VALID Configuration the receiver cannot decode: the published Transfer Format is S24LE (well-formed per spec) but this Client cannot decode 24-bit — it answers Error(403)+Close(403).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (READY: Subscribe with unhealthy capture -> Error(501, retryable=true); no state change)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (error response classes: 501 is a non-fatal instance)
cases.summary: Subscribe while the Endpoint capture is unhealthy/absent: non-fatal Error(501, retryable=true) — connection kept, state stays READY; the Client may retry after the next ConfigurationPublished.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (PLAYING: capture failed -> push StreamEnded(501, retryable=true))
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.4 (StreamEnded carries code + detail, no Status)
cases.summary: Capture fails mid-stream: the Server pushes StreamEnded(501) — state PLAYING -> READY; diagnostics counters survive for finalization.
Normal capture end: StreamEnded(502) push moves the session PLAYING -> READY.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (any: fatal error raised -> matching Error + Close)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (error payload <= 512 B post-auth; detail <= 256 B, TM-7)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.2 (detail rules: no secrets, paths, or stack traces)
cases.summary: Internal Server error while processing a request, shown at the maximum detail size (256 bytes): Error(599) + Close(599), with the post-auth payload bound asserted.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §3 (idle timeout 30 s -> classify 601; transport close carries the registry code)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (any: idle timeout -> transport close carrying 601)
cases.summary: Idle timeout (30 s of silence, keep-alives failing): NO control frames — the QUIC application close carries code 601; the Client classifies 601 and reconnects with backoff.
The transport cannot carry media: no QUIC DATAGRAM support, or the datagram limit is below header + one frame — the Server sends Close(602).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.3 (Close: both directions; one-way, never echoed)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (READY/PLAYING: Close received -> no echo; CLOSING)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.3 (CLOSING: final diagnostics, then transport close)
cases.summary: Normal Client stop: the Client sends Close(701) and must expect NO response frames — Close is never echoed; the receiver's transport close is the acknowledgment.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.1 (flags: STREAM_START on the first datagram)
cases.summary: Baseline media datagrams with every header field exercised: STREAM_START on sequence 0 / timestamp 0, then the next datagram with all fields advanced. Payload = 8 stereo F32LE sample frames (64 B).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.1 (flags table: bit 2 SPARE — receiver MUST ignore)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §12 (parked: reserved flag bits ignored (not rejected), accepted with D4)
cases.summary: A datagram with a reserved flag bit set (bit 2, 0x4) is processed normally — reserved bits are IGNORED, never rejected and never treated as malformed.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.2 (receivers maintain an RFC 3550 §A.1 extended 64-bit sequence with cycle folding)
cases.summary: Sequence wrap: the last datagram of instance 3 carries sequence 0xffffffff; the next carries 0x00000000 — the receiver folds the cycle, extending the sequence to 2^32.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (PLAYING: capture restart -> StreamEnded(502), then StreamStarted(new instance))
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.2 (new instance id on every capture reset/restart; receiver epoch reset)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.5 (new instance id: begin a new receiver epoch)
cases.summary: Capture restart: the reliable control stream announces the end of instance 1 and the start of instance 2, then the first media datagram of instance 2 arrives with STREAM_START; the receiver resets playback and statistics state.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (PLAYING: decode-affecting config change -> generation +1, push ConfigurationPublished)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.1 (flags: CONFIG_CHANGE on the first datagram of a greater generation)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.6 (unknown configuration: bounded hold, then drop)
cases.summary: Decode-affecting change mid-stream (48 kHz -> 96 kHz): generation increments 1 -> 2 inside the SAME instance, the reliable ConfigurationPublished push announces it, and media switches generation — including a stale gen-1 datagram that must be dropped, never decoded with either config.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.3 (payload_max = max_datagram_size() − 24, re-queried at send time, D2)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §2 D2 (prototype: mds 1192 at path MTU 1280)
cases.summary: Reduced path MTU (DPLPMTUD converged at mds = 1192, the value the prototype observed at path MTU 1280): payload_max = 1168 = 146 whole F32LE stereo frames — the datagram is sized to the CURRENT limit at send time.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.3 (frames per datagram = floor(payload_max / frame_bytes); payload always frame-aligned)
cases.summary: Payload alignment under an awkward limit: with mds = 1165, payload_max = 1141, so the sender sends floor(1141 / 8) = 142 frames = 1136 bytes — the 5-byte remainder is never sent as a partial sample frame.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.3 (interop floor: every implementation MUST accept media payloads up to 1176 bytes = 1200 − 24)
cases.summary: Interop floor: a datagram with exactly 1176 payload bytes (147 F32LE stereo frames; 1200-byte datagram) must be accepted by every receiver, whatever its local maximum.
Malformed media is dropped SILENTLY (no wire response exists for datagrams): an impossible instance id (0) and a payload that is not frame-aligned.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §3 (framing: length == 0 or > 65536 -> 401; 64 KiB is the cap, not 64 KiB − 1)
cases.summary: Boundary: a frame whose length is EXACTLY 65536 passes the framing check (only > 65536 violates) and is processed — here a Subscribe plus an unknown padding field, answered with SubscribeResponse(OK).

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.2 (pre-auth responses carry no detail; <= 128 B)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (general pre-auth responses <= 128 B — challenges, rejections, errors; TM-6 revised)
cases.summary: The 128 B pre-auth response boundary: the three pre-auth response shapes (AuthChallenge, AuthResult(202), AuthResult(204)) with their exact sizes — all without any detail field.

spec: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §4.2 (the sole exception: successful PairingResponse <= 320 B Frame.length)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (successful PairingResponse <= 320 B Frame.length; TM-6 revised)
cases.summary: The 320 B PairingResponse boundary: the successful QR PairingResponse from the pairing happy path, byte-exact, with its total framed size asserted against the 320 B cap.
